description_en: Ugratārā is located 5 kilometres north of Amargadhi, Dadeldhura's district headquarters. It is reached via the Mahakali Highway.The temple is the main focus of a large Hindu complexe, metonymically known as Ugratārā. The monument is built on a circular mound and is accessed by two flight of stairs. The temple is oriented to the east. It is constituted of two rooms. The first one, to the east, is a large vestibule that one may access through doors located to the east and the south. On the western side of the room is a door leading to the second, western room, thesanctum(was not accessed during survey). The whole temple is a modern construction from the second half of the 20th century but it contained different types of medieval artefacts.One important medieval artefact is a horizontal stone frieze placed underneath the threshold of thesanctum. The object (001) represents lions and devotees turned towards a central sitted goddess. This goddess is localy identified as Ugratārā or as Kālikā. Next is a pair of stone pillars that were originally part of a smallśikharatemple or a pavilion. These pillars (002) are installed together inside a niche, on the southern wall of thesanctum. According to the local lore these pillars were used during human sacrifices (narabali). Before the entrance to the temple, to the south directly after the stairs, is a small Bhairava Mandira where stone images of various origin and styles are kept (003). Before the stairs, to the south, is a stone memorial pillar (004) where buffaloes are sacrificed. This is one of the rare memorial pillars encountered in the district and it may date from the 13th-15th century. Goats are sacrificed at another place, located north of the temple and marked by a small shrine containing a modern statue of Kālī (005).Nothing is known regarding the history of the site. Yet the medieval artefacts found there may indicate that it was already a place of worship around the 13th-15th century. The site is described inSharma 2012(pp. 329-331).The temple of Ugratārā is visited daily by Hindu worshippers from Dadeldhura and the nearby districts.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
